newsitem.title: USA: Washington mayor says he needs 31 bodyguards.
newsitem.headline: Washington mayor says he needs 31 bodyguards.

text.p: Washington Mayor Marion Barry is fighting to keep the city council from trimming his 31-member bodyguard detail, far bigger than the guard for the mayor of any other American city, aides said Thursday.

While the mayors of similarly-sized Seattle and New Orleans get by with two bodyguards, Barry is "an extremely controversial and highly visible" politician who needs the extra round-the-clock protection, his chief of staff said.
In a letter to the city council, Barry Campbell cited "stacks" of threatening letters and a recent bomb threat against the four-term mayor.

In a city awash in diplomats and well-known politicians who travel unguarded and little noticed, Barry makes his rounds with a police-car-led entourage that rivals visiting heads of state. The detail also guards his wife and son.

Criticism by members of a financial control board appointed by Congress to rescue the near-bankrupt city has led the council to consider cutting back the number of bodyguards, all members of the police department. A council committee has voted to cut in half the $1.2 million a year allocated for the guard detail, but the full council must approve the plan.
In 1977, Barry was shot in the chest by a shotgun pellet when a group of Hanafi Muslims seized the District Building, Washington's former city hall.
